university: SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry

documents.title: Generative AI at ESF
documents.summary: A short IT-hosted page that frames generative AI as a tool users must review and make their own, recommends entering college data only in approved tools, and lists AI tools and learning resources. It sets no academic-integrity or classroom rules.
documents.stance_why: The page states no rule on whether students may use AI for coursework; it only says "It is our responsibility to review and revise AI-generated content" and lists approved tools, so it sets no course-use stance and leaves that decision to others (delegates).

units.why: The sentence says "It is our responsibility to review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy", which sets a duty on all users to check AI output, so it is verify-output (P31). The added "make it our own" touches P29 (ownership), but verification is the main point and the ownership clause is not framed as a rule for submitted work.
units.anchor: review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy and make it our own.
units.fit_note: Also says users should make the content their own (ownership), which P31 does not capture alone.

units.why: "Generative AI requires human input, editing, and evaluation" states that a human must stay in the loop, so users remain the ones who do the thinking and judging (P32). It is a general principle, hence phase general and modality informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI requires human input, editing, and evaluation.

units.why: "These tools generate new content based on existing data from the internet or other databases" defines what generative AI is for the page, so it sets scope (P61) and informs rather than directs.
units.anchor: These tools generate new content based on existing data from the internet or other databases
units.fit_note: Definition also notes that tools may draw on user or College data, a privacy fact.

units.why: The text recommends "users should only enter SUNY ESF data when working in the following approved generative AI tools", which limits where college data may go and prefers vetted tools that "meet security and compliance standards" (P50). The modality is should because it says "recommended".
units.anchor: should only enter SUNY ESF data when working in the following approved generative AI tools
units.frag_start: It is recommended that users should

units.why: The page lists Microsoft Co-Pilot, Google Gemini, Adobe Express, Claude and Mentor.AI under "Tools for Students, Faculty, and Staff", so the college provides sanctioned AI tools (P17). It is an offer of access, so modality informs and unit stance permit.
units.anchor: Tools for Students, Faculty, and Staff
units.frag_start: Tools for Students, Faculty, and Staff
units.policy: ESF provides Microsoft Co-Pilot, Google Gemini (with SU Net ID), Adobe Express, Claude and Mentor.AI as AI tools for students, faculty and staff.
units.fit_note: Tools are provided institution-wide, not course-specific, and include agentic coding (Claude Code), relevant to P07.

units.why: The page points users to the "Google AI Fundamentals course offered for free as part of a partnership between SUNY and Google", offering AI-literacy training to the community (P70). It is an offer, not a requirement, so may.
units.anchor: Take the Google AI Fundamentals course
units.policy: Users are invited to take the Google AI Fundamentals course, offered free through a SUNY and Google partnership.

units.why: The Moon library guide is described as giving "a history of AI, guidance on how to ask better questions, evaluating AI resources, and information on AI in academia", an AI-literacy resource (P70). It is a pointer, so informs.
units.anchor: a history of AI, guidance on how to ask better questions, evaluating AI resources
units.policy: ESF points users to the Moon library guide for a history of AI, guidance on asking better questions, evaluating AI resources, and AI in academia.

units.why: The page directs users to the "KnowBe4 training library" on "AI's impact on technology and cybersecurity", a training offer; closest type is P70 (training), though P75 covers security threats, which the text does not name as phishing.
units.anchor: Learn about AI's impact on technology and cybersecurity
units.policy: Users are pointed to the SUNY ESF KnowBe4 training library to learn about AI's impact on technology and cybersecurity.
units.fit_note: The training is on cybersecurity impacts of AI, not general AI literacy.

notes: Only a thin IT page; no academic-integrity AI policy. Stance delegates is a default since the page says nothing about coursework use.
